title: Rectangular prism
spec: To construct a rectangular prism, start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to -90.0, 0.0, and -90.0 degrees, and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the plane defined by this coordinate system. The first face, Face 1, consists of a loop made up of four lines. Line 1 starts at (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.0417, 0.0). Line 2 starts at (0.0417, 0.0) and ends at (0.0417, 0.0972). Line 3 starts at (0.0417, 0.0972) and ends at (0.0, 0.0972). Finally, Line 4 starts at (0.0, 0.0972) and ends at (0.0, 0.0). After drawing the sketch, apply a scaling factor of 0.0972 to it. Then, rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. To transform the sketch into a three-dimensional model, extrude the two-dimensional sketch along its normal by 0.75 units, ensuring that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. This process will create a new solid body with dimensions of 0.0417 units in length, 0.0972 units in width, and 0.75 units in height. The final shape is a cylindrical rod with a rectangular cross-section at one end, featuring a uniform diameter and a smooth surface.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0417, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0417, 0.0972) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0972) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
